key_insight: A GP-compatible metric called EWACS enabled Bayesian temperature tuning of GPT-5.2 to substantially improve agreement with expert Naranjo causality assessments in pharmacovigilance cases.
clinical_relevance: This suggests LLMs may become more useful for screening and supporting causality assessment in adverse event reports, especially when tuned per case rather than using a fixed temperature.
method: Experts labeled 723 stratified FAERS ICSRs using the Naranjo algorithm.
GPT-5.2 was tested with chain-of-thought prompting across temperatures from 0 to 2.
Four composite optimization metrics were compared with Bayesian optimization using a Gaussian Process surrogate and Probability of Improvement.
evidence_signal: On the abstracted evaluation, GPT-5.2 reached 74.1% agreement on Naranjo question 5 and 65.4% on question 10 at baseline, and EWACS-guided optimization raised overall causality agreement from 45.0% to 72.0%.
watch_item: The reported gains come from a single model and dataset, so external validation is needed before using temperature optimization in real pharmacovigilance workflows.
paper_title: Optimizing Large Language Models for Causality Assessment in Pharmacovigilance: Developing a Performance Metric as Objective for Bayesian Hyperparameter Optimization
